literal: Standing before those who know their duty and have a heart without concealment, even begging possesses a unique beauty.
translation: Standing and asking for help before those who know their duty and possess a heart free from withholding has a unique beauty of its own.
modern: ஒளித்துவைக்கும் குணம் இல்லாத நெஞ்சத்தையும், தம் கடமையை அறியும் தன்மையையும் உடையவர் முன்னே நின்று இரந்து கேட்பதும் ஒரு தனி அழகைப் பெற்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains that asking for help is not always a matter of shame; it can have its own grace under the right circumstances. When a person stands and asks (இரப்பும்) before those who do not hide what they have (கரப்பிலா நெஞ்சின்) and who understand their social duty to give (கடனறிவார்), the act of asking becomes dignified. The beauty (ஏஎர்) of this interaction lies in the mutual understanding between a needy person and a generous, dutiful giver. Thus, the poet elevates the act of seeking help when it is directed at the truly noble.
